title: Tenant cost-query sandbox, priority routing, and onboarding playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Large enterprise tenants frequently request ad-hoc, high-cardinality cost queries and scheduled exports (daily/weekly) for internal chargeback and forecasting. These requests often overload upstream billing pipelines, cause unpredictable query latency for other tenants, and require manual triage by PM/SE to determine priority. We need a structured intake + sandbox + routing policy that enables self-serve for low-risk exports, a fast path for SLAd tenants, and guardrails for cost/latency-sensitive workloads.

Goals:
- Provide a 'Cost Query Sandbox' where tenants can prototype and validate exports without touching production billing jobs (fast, isolated compute and sample datasets).
- Define priority lanes and automated routing rules so that enterprise SLA customers get deterministic delivery windows while self-serve requests are rate-limited and scheduled during off-peak.
- Create an onboarding playbook and acceptance checklist for Solutions Engineers to triage requests quickly and migrate validated queries to scheduled exports.
- Reduce manual PM/SE triage time by 60% and reduce billing pipeline overload incidents related to ad-hoc exports by 80% within 3 months of rollout.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Intake form: Extended structured ask inside Console that captures: business use case, data scope, desired cadence, sensitivity level, expected row/column cardinality, and urgency. Route automatically to lanes: self-serve, concierge (SE-assisted), or SLA (enterprise). Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CONSOLE/Cost+Export+Intake+Form
2) Sandbox environment: A per-tenant ephemeral workspace with sampled datasets (1-5% of production or synthetic equivalent), query quota, and estimated cost estimator. Users confirm result shape and runtime in sandbox before requesting a full export. Sandbox uses lower-priority compute pool and returns sample metric estimates.
3) Priority routing: Rules engine that maps attributes (workspace tier, contract SLA, urgency, estimated cost) to scheduling lanes. SLA lane supports guaranteed windows and retries; self-serve lane receives daily scheduling with soft quotas and cost caps.
4) Onboarding playbook + checklist: Step-by-step SE/PM checklist to validate queries, sanitize PII, set up encryption keys for exports (KMS), and create monitoring dashboards (Looker/Console).

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- Intake form deployed in Console and persisting structured metadata in tickets (no free-text only).
- Sandbox can run a sample cost export and return estimated time and token/cost projection within 10 minutes for 95% of sample queries.
- Routing rules applied correctly for 95% of historical backlog replay (we'll run a replay job against last 90 days of intake requests).
- Documentation and onboarding playbook published and a 2-week SE pilot completed with at least two enterprise customers.
- Monitoring: new Looker dashboard showing intake volume, lane assignment, average time-to-commit, and failed-run reasons.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Freshness vs cost: Sandbox returns sampled data to keep costs low; full exports will be scheduled for off-peak windows which may add latency.
- Isolation complexity: Per-tenant ephemeral compute reduces blast radius but adds infra overhead; will require Eng budget for a dedicated sandbox pool.
- RBAC & security: Exports must support customer KMS integration and audit logging; adds extra implementation time and security review.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Asha Patel (owner), Liam Chen (assignee)
comments: 2025-11-06 — Initial scoping meeting with SEs and Sales. SEs reported ~18 manual triages per week for large tenants; average turnaround 3 business days.

2025-11-10 — Engineering feasibility sync: Eng estimates 3 sprints to build a minimal sandbox with sampled datasets and a lightweight scheduler. Concern raised about KV cache reuse hitting sandbox vs prod; suggested dedicated sandbox pools.

2025-11-12 — Design review: DES provided wireframes for sandbox UI and intake form. Feedback: show cost-estimate inline and require data sensitivity tag. Link to mocks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMockUI
2025-11-14 — Legal & Security: Security requested KMS integration and audit log schema; flagged for security review once PR is ready. Note: avoid shipping without KMS for enterprise lane.
2025-11-18 — PM decision log: Proceed with two-phase rollout: Phase 1 (self-serve sandbox + intake form + routing rules for self-serve/concierge); Phase 2 (SLA lane + KMS + guaranteed windows).

2025-11-20 — Next steps: Create ENG tickets for sandbox infra (ENG-22144), scheduler (ENG-22145), and intake form backend (ENG-22146). Draft SE pilot plan and recruit two pilot customers (Customer A: FintechCorp, Customer B: RetailOne).
review_feedback: ENG (2025-11-10): Recommend a hard quota on sandbox CPU/GPU and automatic throttling; allow owners to request quota increases with justification.
DES (2025-11-12): Please include an inline example export schema and sample output in the sandbox UI to reduce support back-and-forth.
SEC (2025-11-14): KMS integration mandatory for enterprise lane; audit logs must include user, workspace, query id, and export destination hash.
open_questions: What is the acceptable sample percentage for sandbox data that balances fidelity vs cost (1% vs 5% vs synthetic)?
How do we enforce tenant-level cost caps if a scheduled export exceeds the estimate? Do we fail or queue?
What SLAs do we commit to for the SLA lane (latency/throughput/retries)?
